methodology: Private static review of client selection DOM guards, selected-message lookup, command registration and code-block resolution. Only authored descriptions and archive-local source ordinals are published.

stages.operation: The range must be noncollapsed, belong to a connected assistant-message-style Markdown container, and have both ends within that same container.
The containing wrapper must have a source-message identity and its conversation identity must match the selected conversation.
The selected range must not intersect writing blocks, learning components, contenteditable regions, or nodes marked to exclude Markdown copying.
The popover looks up the attributed message from scoped conversation mapping; the expanded-details action additionally requires assistant authorship and a valid selected-message record.
The handler can pass selected text and its source message identity to a supplied callback. An optional source-occurrence index is calculated by comparing the range against matching text nodes.
Eligible alternate actions can dynamically import a work-side chat or explanatory side-panel handler with selected text and source message context.

limitations: The selection range validator applies to this popover path; other copy actions may follow different rules.
The source shows guarded callbacks and lazy side-panel imports but not observed user selection or side-panel opening.
The expanded-details eligibility gate does not establish that the ordinary selected-text callback requires the same author or feature flags.

stages.operation: Command enablement is scoped to an allowed conversation origin and feature/copy flags; unsupported origins return no eligible code block.
The resolver walks derived turns and their items in reverse display order and considers assistant-message items for code candidates.
It scans the assistant item's content for code blocks and structured code references; when available it prefers separately resolved code-block content over basic rendered text.
The chosen content carries a source message identity and a code-block index. For referenced code, it derives the index relative to matching source message identities.

If code text is already available, the command copies it immediately; otherwise an eligible in-progress remote item may trigger asynchronous history/content loading before a second resolution attempt.
The asynchronous request uses an AbortController and watches conversation-origin, selected-node, comparison selection and command configuration changes, cancelling on invalidation.
The client delegates text or a promise to a clipboard helper, records a copy-request telemetry event, and can show a success notification after the helper reports completion.

limitations: It resolves the last eligible assistant code block along derived rendered turns, not an unconditional code block from every stored mapping node.
Client clipboard helper calls, telemetry and toasts are statically visible; a successful system clipboard write is not observed.
Asynchronous content loading is guarded by streaming, server-item completeness and current selection; it need not run for every code block.

unverified: Actual browser selection or code-copy gesture, popup visibility, clipboard permission and operating-system clipboard result.
The full implementations of lazy side-panels, separately imported copy helpers, and remote history/content fetching.
Server storage, current deployment feature flags and behavior of message types other than those inspected.
privacy: No captured HTML, JavaScript snippets, string contents, customer identities, original source filenames, request paths or clipboard payloads are published.
